title: ReSIDS adaptation event
description: One observability event emitted by the ReSIDS adaptation plane. Served as an element of GET /events (REST pull) and pushed to the monitor as CoAP telemetry (values object).

seq.description: Monotonic, unique event sequence number (continues across runs).

ts.description: Event timestamp, ISO-8601 UTC with microseconds (REST). When pushed as CoAP/ThingsBoard telemetry it is converted to epoch milliseconds in the enclosing envelope.

round.description: LOCAL round: the tick count of the node-local Disaster-FD cadence, which counts detect_lag and the watchdog D. The time reference comes from Disaster-FD; the agent infers no time from the traffic. (In the scenario simulations it is re-indexed over the windows the scenario selects.)

fed_round.description: FEDERATED round: the tick count of the regional Disaster-FD cadence (one federated tick every N local rounds), which counts dwell and cmd_latency and is the only cadence at which federated decisions are taken.

traffic_time_start.description: Optional, profile-dependent: time of the FIRST traffic frame scored in the window, when the protocol carries one (IEC 61850 GOOSE/SV). For correlation with sequence-of-event records. Absent where the data has no time (CICIoT2023). Never used to define the window.

traffic_time_end.description: Optional, profile-dependent: time of the LAST traffic frame scored in the window. See traffic_time_start.

from_mode.description: Previous aggregation mode (architecture_change only; null otherwise).

to_mode.description: New aggregation mode (architecture_change only; null otherwise).

reason.description: CAUSE of the event; who decided is in decided_by. architecture_change: node_failure | recovery | scheduled | intrusion | autonomous_fallback. node_failure: node_failure. node_recovery: recovery. node_isolated: intrusion. 'autonomous_fallback' marks the agent's watchdog: its node-local Disaster-FD monitor was unavailable for D rounds, so the agent switched FL->GL on its own (always with decided_by=autonomous). 'commanded' is retained for compatibility with streams produced before 1.5.0 and is not emitted any more: the decider is stated by decided_by, the cause by this field.

failed_nodes.description: Logical node indices identified as failing (authoritative on node_failure; context on architecture_change).

active_nodes.description: Node indices participating this round, or null when all are active.

attack.description: intrusion_detected (and node_isolated): the attack label, drawn from the label set of the domain profile in force (reported by /status and the manifest; docs/PROFILES.md) -- e.g. 'injection' in the iec61850-goose-sv profile's ereno-7 set, 'DDoS' in iot-flow's ciciot2023-7. The core does not fix a vocabulary. Null otherwise.

k_votes.description: intrusion_detected only: number of concurring specialists (the k in k-of-n) that raised the alarm — the corroboration strength.

n_flags.description: intrusion_detected only: number of samples/flows flagged in this round/window (alarm volume).

source_node.description: intrusion_detected (and node_isolated): the node whose traffic the alarm is attributed to. Where that identity comes from is fixed by the domain profile (docs/PROFILES.md): the protocol's publisher identity (in iec61850-goose-sv, the GOOSE/SV APPID, gocbRef or source MAC), a device address, or nothing -- profile attribution 'none', in which case it is always null. Null whenever attribution is unavailable, which is the case in v2 outside the synthetic scenarios.

detector_specialists.description: intrusion_detected only: indices of the SPECIALISTS (boosters) in the local pool that fired. Not nodes: every node holds the same diffused union and reaches the same verdict, so what varies is which specialists fired.

recovered_nodes.description: node_recovery only: logical node indices that came back.

mode.description: Aggregation mode in effect for this event, so the monitor never infers state.

n_active.description: Number of active nodes when the event was emitted (len(active_nodes)).

window_start.description: Start of the window: the node-local Disaster-FD tick at which it opened (synthetic epoch under simulation). The window is whatever the agent scored between two ticks; it is NOT derived from traffic timestamps -- those, when the profile has them, are in traffic_time_start/end. Distinct from ts, which is the emission instant.

window_end.description: End of the window: the next node-local Disaster-FD tick (exclusive).

window_samples.description: Samples the agent scored between the two local ticks -- the denominator for n_flags. The window length is not fixed (Disaster-FD may stretch its cadence under delay), so triage needs both n_flags and the fraction n_flags / window_samples: measured, a rule combining them and calibrated at 1 s holds when the tick is stretched to 10 s, but neither is invariant when it is shortened (scripts/cadence_sweep.py).

decided_by.description: Who took the ACTION. Present only on events that ARE an action: architecture_change and node_isolated. Pure observations (node_failure, node_recovery, intrusion_detected) carry no decision and omit it. 'monitor' = a Disaster-FD monitor process (one per node and per server): the NODE-LOCAL instance for the fail-fast FL->GL on inactivity (local evidence, no regional quorum), the FEDERATED Disaster-FD for everything else (losses while in GL, intrusion-driven isolation, the GL->FL return). 'autonomous' = the ReSIDS agent acting alone, which happens ONLY as its watchdog FL->GL (reason autonomous_fallback) when its own node-local Disaster-FD process is unavailable -- the fail-safe direction only. 'operator' is retained for a human decision recorded through Disaster-FD.

command_id.description: The command that caused this action, when one did (docs/COMMANDS.md). Present only where decided_by is 'monitor' or 'operator'; null or absent on the agent's watchdog action, which no command caused. This field is what closes the loop between the two surfaces: the command result can be lost in transit, so the EVENT carrying command_id is the authoritative commit record, and the Disaster-FD monitor correlates on it rather than trusting its response.
